sections.heading: Properties of integers and number classification

questions.q: Classify the number $-\dfrac{7}{2}$ as an integer, rational number, or irrational number.
questions.answer: $-\dfrac{7}{2}=-3.5$ is a rational number (it can be expressed as a ratio of two integers), but it is NOT an integer, since it is not a whole number.

sections.heading: Percent of a percent (successive percent changes)

questions.q: A jacket is marked down 30%, then an additional 10% is taken off the sale price. If the original price was 100 dollars, find the final price.
questions.answer: After the first discount: $100(0.70)=70$ dollars. After the second discount: $70(0.90)=63$ dollars.

questions.q: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 3:5. If there are 40 students total, find the number of boys.
questions.answer: Total ratio parts: $3+5=8$. Each part represents $\dfrac{40}{8}=5$ students. Boys: $3\times5=15$.

questions.q: A recipe uses a ratio of 2 cups flour to 3 cups sugar. If a baker uses 15 cups of sugar, how much flour is needed?
questions.answer: Set up a proportion: $\dfrac{2}{3}=\dfrac{x}{15}$. Cross-multiply: $3x=30$, so $x=10$ cups of flour.

sections.heading: Word problems involving rates and mixtures

questions.q: A store mixes 4 pounds of candy costing 3 dollars per pound with 6 pounds of candy costing 5 dollars per pound. Find the average price per pound of the mixture.
questions.answer: Total cost: $4(3)+6(5)=12+30=42$ dollars. Total weight: $4+6=10$ pounds. Average price: $\dfrac{42}{10}=4.20$ dollars per pound.

sections.heading: Combining percent, ratio, and rate concepts

questions.q: This question has two parts. A store buys a product for 40 dollars and marks it up 60% to set the retail price. (a) Find the retail price. (b) If the store later offers a 25% discount off the retail price, find the discounted price, and determine whether the store still makes a profit compared to its 40-dollar cost.
questions.answer: (a) Markup amount: $40(0.60)=24$ dollars. Retail price: $40+24=64$ dollars. (b) Discount amount: $64(0.25)=16$ dollars. Discounted price: $64-16=48$ dollars. Since $48>40$, the store still makes a profit of $48-40=8$ dollars per item.

sections.heading: A multi-step number theory and ratio problem

questions.q: This question has two parts. A recipe for 12 cookies requires a ratio of 3 cups flour to 2 cups sugar to 1 cup butter. (a) Find the amount of each ingredient needed to make 30 cookies. (b) If flour costs 0.60 dollars per cup, sugar costs 0.80 dollars per cup, and butter costs 1.50 dollars per cup, find the total ingredient cost for 30 cookies.
questions.answer: (a) Scale factor: $\dfrac{30}{12}=2.5$. Flour: $3\times2.5=7.5$ cups. Sugar: $2\times2.5=5$ cups. Butter: $1\times2.5=2.5$ cups. (b) Total cost: $7.5(0.60)+5(0.80)+2.5(1.50)=4.5+4+3.75=12.25$ dollars.
